channel.title: Kinetic Code — Digital Engineering Craft
channel.description: The technical journal of a mechatronics engineer: embedded systems, industrial automation and software, explained the way you would explain them out loud.

item.title: Optimizing matrix multiplication in C++ — Part 3: vectorization, the full reveal, and two honest surprises
item.description: The final part of the series: hand-writing AVX2 + FMA vector instructions to squeeze four multiply-adds into one, the full five-stage comparison from 1.88 to 11.49 GFLOP/s, and two measured surprises — a power-of-two matrix size that runs 6.5x slower than its neighbors, and a 2.12x speedup that costs zero lines of code.

item.title: Optimizing matrix multiplication in C++ — Part 2: tiling, threads, and one honest surprise
item.description: Part 2 of the hands-on performance engineering series: why splitting the matrices into small cache-sized tiles doesn't automatically pay off on its own, and how putting a second CPU core to work with a single OpenMP pragma pushes us to a measured 4.42x — all verified, all reproducible.

item.title: Optimizing matrix multiplication in C++ — Part 1: what the loop order actually buys you
item.description: The first article in a hands-on series on performance engineering: why matrix multiplication is slow by default, how a computer's memory really works, and how reordering three for loops alone buys a 2.2x speedup — measured, not assumed.

item.title: Industrial optics fundamentals: what actually matters when you pick a lens
item.description: A practical primer on machine vision optics — field of view, working distance, depth of field, focal length, mounts, F-number, and the trade-offs that decide whether an inspection system actually works.

item.title: Redirecting Qt qDebug to a file without recompiling: the LoggerManager class
item.description: A crash in the field I could not diagnose, no way to recompile on the spot, and the C++/Qt class I wrote to catch logs at runtime — with every linking error I hit along the way.

item.title: How to Autostart a Program on Windows
item.description: Do you have a program that you want to open automatically every time you start your computer? In this short guide, we will see how to do it quickly and easily using a built-in Windows tool called Task Scheduler.

item.title: Building a Personal Expense Tracker from Scratch: Architecture and Database Design (Part 3)
item.description: This article retraces the design and development process of a personal expense tracking web application. The goal isn't just to create a working tool, but to analyze every engineering decision and understand the 'why' behind our technological choices.
